newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: French actress Adjani to settle in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: French actress Adjani to settle in Geneva.

text.p: Actress Isabelle Adjani has joined the ranks of French film stars who have chosen to live in Geneva, where they enjoy lower taxes as well as privacy.
The 41-year-old, in an interview with the daily Tribune de Geneve on Tuesday, said the Swiss lakeside city offered her 16-month-old son Gabriel-Kane cleaner air than Paris.
Adjani, noting her maternal grandfather was from Zurich and her elder son Barnabe attends summer camp in the Swiss Alps, also said her mother wanted to live part-time in Switzerland.
"My coming to Geneva can be placed under the sign of a family regrouping," Adjani was quoted as saying.

"I love Paris and will continue to love it and go there regularly. But the pollution has become too bad, especially during the summer. The situation there worries me for my son, Gabriel-Kane. Living in Geneva is a solution which gives me breathing space in all meanings of the word," she added.

Adjani, who co-starred with Sharon Stone in the thriller "Diabolique" and opposite compatriot Gerard Depardieu in "Claudel", has been granted a residence permit by Geneva's authorities, according to her lawyer Dominique Warluzel.

"Contrary to popular thought, Geneva is not a fiscal paradise. Having said that, it is true generally that taxes on income and personal fortune are less high in Switzerland than in France," Warluzel was quoted as saying.

French actor Alain Delon resides with his Dutch wife and two young children in Geneva. Other Frenchmen residing in the Geneva area are Formula One racers Alain Prost and Jean Alesi, writer Frederic Dard and singer Charles Aznavour.
"The most brilliant French actress leaves Paris for our city," the Tribune de Geneve boasted in a front-page story.
"In moving to Geneva, Isabelle Adjani wants to offer her children a more peaceful and healthy life," it added.

Adjani came to international attention with her role in the 1974 film "Story of Adele H" by Francois Truffaut, for which she received an Oscar nomination. She got her fourth French "Cesar" award as best actress for her role in the 1994 film "Margot".
